title: The first belt
text: Billy's Snooki's Cookie went 11-2 and led the league in points, scoring 23% above the weekly league median. The roster was built almost entirely at the draft (86% of started points from his own picks), headlined by eighth-round Patrick Mahomes (379 SP) and second-round Travis Kelce, giving him the league's best QB (+7.7 per week over average) and TE (+12.2) production. After a first-round bye he beat Joey 107.8–78.6, catching Joey 56 points below his season average, then took the final over Tyler 179.4–135.8.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons

title: Back-to-back on a lucky bounce
text: Billy repeated despite only the fifth-best scoring offense: his 10-3 record came 2.4 wins above what his scores deserved, the most luck in the league. His running backs ranked 13th of 14, so the title ran through the receivers (2nd), led by Michael Thomas's 337 started points, and two week-6 trades that brought in Stefon Diggs, Josh Jacobs and Jared Cook (19% of his started points came via trade). In the playoffs he edged Tyler 109.6–104.5, with Tyler 15 points under his average, then beat Jake 146.7–120.0 in the final.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons, Trade Ledger

title: The midseason rebuild
text: Hayden's first title came from a midseason turnaround: below the league median through the first half, then the second-best scoring team the rest of the way. First-round pick Christian McCaffrey gave him only 90 started points, so he rebuilt by trade, landing Travis Kelce from Jake in week 4 (229 SP) and Terry McLaurin from Joey in week 7, plus free agent Myles Gaskin (123 SP). Only half his started points came from his own draft picks, the lowest share in the league. Patrick Mahomes was again the league's top QB (+5.1 per week), luck added 2.3 wins (most in the league), and he closed it out over Bryce 117.3–113.5 and Harlan 124.7–110.1.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons, Trade Ledger

title: Three titles, by 0.78 points
text: Billy's third belt was built on the league's best backfield and quarterback: Najee Harris and Ezekiel Elliott gave him +10.6 points per week at RB, Josh Allen came in the fourth round, and third-round Cooper Kupp scored 434 started points, the best value pick in league history. A modest 8-6 record (0.9 wins unlucky) made him the 4 seed, but he got hot in the playoffs: 125.5–102.4 over Bryce, a 161.6–64.7 rout of Nick, then a 139.3–138.5 win over Joey in the final, decided by 0.78 points.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons, Draft Grades

title: Wire to wire
text: Griffin's Tsutomu Yamaguchi was the best team from start to finish: 9-5, the league's top scorer, and the 1 seed. The engine was a running back room 17.8 points per week better than the league average, the biggest positional edge any champion has had, with first-round Austin Ekeler (350 SP) and fourth-round Josh Jacobs (314 SP). Nearly everything came from the draft (86% of started points). After the bye he won his two playoff games by a combined 110 points: 159.1–108.3 over Harlan and 163.5–103.8 over Nathan.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons

title: The heist
text: Hayden's second title is the most improbable in league history. Bear Force One ranked 11th of 14 in points, scored below the league median for the season, and was 13th in lineup efficiency, but luck turned an expected 5.8 wins into 8-6 and the 6 seed. All three playoff opponents then scored well below their season averages (by 33, 17 and 22 points), and he won those games by 0.88, 39.6 and 1.08 points. Stefon Diggs (269 SP), Amari Cooper and Tony Pollard did the heavy lifting, with waiver pickup C.J. Stroud (week 3, 172 SP) at quarterback.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons

title: The running back room
text: Tyler's first title rode the league's second-best backfield (+13.2 points per week): third-round De'Von Achane, ninth-round Chuba Hubbard (228 SP) and Jahmyr Gibbs, acquired from Chris in week 9 in a trade that netted +112 started points. That more than offset a week-6 deal with Jake that cost him 289. Burnie Xanders finished 10-4 as the 2 seed, scored 11% above the median after midseason, and won the playoffs 163.6–129.3 over Austin Abegg and 122.0–117.5 over Jake.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons, Trade Ledger

title: Back-to-back across platforms
text: Tyler won the first Sleeper season to make it two straight. Unverified Sources started slowly, below the median through the first half, then posted the league's best second half (26% above the median). Josh Allen was the top QB (+5.9 per week) and first-round Jahmyr Gibbs scored 360 started points, while two early trades with Jake, for DK Metcalf in week 2 and A.J. Brown in week 5, added a combined 209 started points of margin. All three playoff opponents fell 20–33 points below their averages: Connor 133.7–95.2, Austin Joannes 157.8–114.4, and Nathan 100.3–83.6 in the final.
source: Team Seasons, Team Weeks, Player Seasons, Trade Ledger
